hero.headline: Jensen Beach Park cafe and restroom rebuild expected by late 2027
hero.teaser: Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The county is currently processing permits and designing the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe.
hero.body:
The restroom and concession building at Jensen Beach Park remains an empty plot of land more than a year after a fire destroyed the facility on New Year's Eve in December 2024. Beachgoer Gonda Ghebert reached out to WPTV's Let's Hear It inbox to report that beachgoers are left with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach and feels it has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Regular visitors say they also miss the cafe itself. Julie Goings said she went to the park because they had a nice, clean facility with showers and it was convenient to get a snack or drink coming off the deck. Sam Elliott said the only thing really missing is concessions and food availability.

Kevin Abbate, the Parks and Recreation director, says the permitting process takes time because the project must go through the Department of Environmental Protection since the site sits on a protected dune. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80% complete. Abbate says the facility will be about 15 feet in elevation with 100 seats and 33 at the bar, providing a good seat for everyone.

The county says final funding is expected to be approved in September. They hope to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county also told WPTV they do not have any plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities in the meantime. Abbate says the cafe will be worth the wait, explaining that they want to do it right and design it properly so when they get through construction, they will have fewer issues and a much smoother process.

Those who use the beach say they are anxiously awaiting construction to begin. Elliott said he is hoping it moves real fast. Goings said she wants the bathrooms up and running and it would be nice to have another little convenient spot at the beach.

cards.headline: 66-year-old Fort Pierce man dies after shooting on Essex Drive in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: The St.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the victim in Tuesday afternoon's shooting on Essex Drive as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Deputies responded around 3:30 p.m. to a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned an adult man had shot another adult man with a rifle.

Deputies took the suspect into custody and began providing emergency medical care to Barnes until St. Lucie County Fire District personnel arrived. Barnes was then taken to a local hospital, where he died. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division are continuing to process evidence, conduct interviews, and work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The suspect remains in custody. Investigators say there is no threat to the public. This is an ongoing investigation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce to overhaul waterfront development process after multiple lawsuits, controversies
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from plaintiff Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of the historic Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has an obligation to defend itself but also believes the lawsuit lacks merit. He said the settlement was not practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. "You can't wait for an election or fund a special election every time you want to do something on city-owned property that's waterfront," Broderick said.

The Little Jim Bait & Tackle case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, the developer of King's Landing threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, developer Chris Shelli of Fisherman's Wharf filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it did not own. In 2025, the city abruptly canceled the Little Jim's lease bidding process after public outcry, prompting Keene's lawsuit and leaving at least two developers frustrated. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant.

Broderick acknowledged the controversies alleged in the lawsuit, which claim a broader pattern of defective administration of city waterfront properties. When asked how the city responds to allegations of mismanaging waterfront properties, Broderick said he would not call it poor management. "I'm not going to say it's managed poorly. I'm going to say it's not being managed, and that's an issue I take very seriously," Broderick said. He told reporters the city plans a top down, bottom up approach to examine the entire portfolio and fix issues one asset at a time.

The city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties with the goal of preventing these problems from happening again. "I will not rest until I get to the bottom of this issue, it's going to be categorized, it's going to be spreadsheeted," Broderick said. Both sides say they are open to negotiating. Keene says he wants transparency, not money, and is willing to revise his offer. Broderick says he will consider any feasible settlement that keeps the case out of court.

cards.headline: 28-year-old man dies after weekend shooting on South 14th Street in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after being shot multiple times early Sunday morning in Fort Pierce. Police said the shooting followed an earlier altercation on Okeechobee Road.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend, according to police. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street. Police said officers arrived at the scene and found two people with apparent gunshot wounds. The 28-year-old man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a local hospital but died from his injuries on Tuesday. Officers also found a 28-year-old woman with injuries to her hand from the shooting, but her injuries were described as not life-threatening. The names of the victims have not been released.

Police said a preliminary investigation indicated that the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation in the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As they arrived home, police said a man believed to be involved in the previous altercation approached and opened fire before fleeing the area. Police said this investigation remains active and ongoing. Anyone with information in the case is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County man approved for experimental pancreatic cancer treatment after 62-day wait
cards.teaser: Russell Reed, 64, of St. Lucie County spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his oncologist believed could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective.
cards.body:
Russell Reed, 64, learned just two days after sharing his story with WPTV that he had been approved to receive daraxonrasib through the FDA's Expanded Access Program. The drug is now in his hands, and his family says he is already feeling better and optimistic about what comes next. Reed had spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved after his oncologist submitted the request, believing the experimental treatment could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective. "Chemotherapy isn't going to help me at this point," Reed said.

Daraxonrasib, also known as RMC-6236, is an investigational once-daily oral pill developed by Revolution Medicines. The drug targets mutated KRAS proteins, which drive more than 90% of pancreatic cancers. While the treatment is not yet FDA-approved, early clinical trial results have generated optimism among some patients and physicians. "There's a lot of anecdotal evidence and a lot of evidence from the clinical trials that show that this is the miracle drug for pancreatic cancer," Reed said. "It is not a cure, but it will give me time." While daraxonrasib is not considered a cure for pancreatic cancer, the Reeds say the approval represents something they've been fighting for all along: more time together.

cards.headline: Vero Beach homeowner may sell home as insurance costs hit $9,000 annually
cards.teaser: Kelly Hagen says her homeowners insurance jumped from $6,000 to $9,000 a year and may force her to sell her Vero Beach home within months if costs continue rising.
cards.body:
Kelly Hagen owns a three bedroom, two bath home in Vero Beach that is about 1,500 square feet and was built in 1994. Her homeowners insurance now costs $9,000 a year, which equals $750 a month on top of her mortgage payment. The premium jumped from $6,000 to $8,000 in one year and has continued climbing. Her insurance company requires impact windows, an expensive upgrade she has struggled to afford while working two jobs. Hagen works a full-time job and also works Instacart nights and weekends to pay for the premiums.

Hagen was turned away for a $10,000 My Safe Florida Home grant after it took too long to find a contractor. She says she can hang on for probably just a couple more months before she will have to try to sell her house. Stand Insurance, a new company in the market, is offering to help homeowners connect with affordable contractors. Stand uses AI technology to study homes and then works to pair homeowners with vendors and contractors to make repairs. Dan Preston, the CEO of Stand Insurance, said helping homeowners be safer is beneficial because the company does not have to pay out in claims and customers pay less in premiums.

cards.headline: Martin County School District to cut 16 administrative positions, save nearly $4 million
cards.teaser: The Martin County School District plans to eliminate 16 administrative and district-level positions, including three assistant principal positions, and remove 42 unfilled instructional vacancies.
cards.body:
The Martin County School District plans to cut staff as part of a reorganization for the upcoming school year, saving nearly $4 million from next year's budget. Superintendent Michael Maine told WPTV the plan includes eliminating 16 administrative and district-level positions, which includes three assistant principal positions, and removing 42 unfilled instructional vacancies. Maine said 10 of those vacancies were held in reserve, contingent on increasing enrollment. Maine said the reorganization is eliminating positions no longer needed at the district office so that the district office bears a majority of the reduction. The changes are expected to save about $3.9 million from the district's projected budget next school year.

Maine said the cuts reflect how the district routinely manages staffing each year by looking at projected student numbers and allocating staff based on those projections. The Martin County School District currently enrolls 16,000 students. Maine said the goal is to protect classroom resources while streamlining operations at the district level. Not everyone is fully on board with the scope of the cuts. Abigal, whose son will be a fourth grader at Jensen Beach Elementary this fall, said she values the small class sizes and close teacher relationships the district currently offers. She said the children need the admin, the teachers, and all the resources they can get.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk website down for hours after third-party redirection issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday morning, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online around 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the website outage that redirected visitors to another site for hours before coming back online by about 1:30 p.m. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider. She assured the public that at no time was personal or confidential information compromised or at risk, noting the clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website.

Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. As soon as he identified the issue, he turned off the site and started the investigation. The clerk's office communications team said this was not a hack because there was not any personal information compromised. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said the payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available, with only the main page affected. The office is working to prevent similar issues, and Clavijo said as soon as they identify the exact issue, there will be a tremendous remediation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce owes state nearly $16,000 for operating docks without permits since 2021
cards.teaser: Documents from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection show Fort Pierce has been operating docks on state-owned submerged land at Little Jim Bait & Tackle without required permits since 2021.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection has ordered Fort Pierce to pay nearly $16,000 by July 17 for operating docks on state-owned submerged land at Little Jim Bait & Tackle without required permits since 2021. The FDEP action, issued in June, comes amid a lawsuit filed by local resident Kevin Keene over the city's handling of the waterfront property. City Commissioner Michael Broderick acknowledged the permit issue, confirming that someone at some point extended the docks further than allowed. He plans to negotiate the fines down while the city investigates who authorized the extension, noting that Fort Pierce owns the real estate and is ultimately the responsible party.

The dispute traces back to last year when the Fort Pierce landmark of nearly 80 years faced an uncertain future after its lease expired. The city offered up the land lease for bidders, prompting outcry from residents. After an outpouring of community support, the city kept the restaurant open month to month. Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer in Keene's lawsuit. Under the proposed terms, Keene would have dropped the case if the city halted new plans for Little Jim until FDEP permit issues are resolved and allowed a public vote on future waterfront land decisions.

hero.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt in World Cup quarterfinals
hero.body:
Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to a 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time remaining. The defending champions will face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri.

Messi scored his record-extending 21st World Cup goal in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks after Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. Egypt had led 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Fernandez said after the match that his team never gives up and that four years have passed since Qatar. He added that Argentina came to enjoy another World Cup and wants to win it again. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni praised his players afterward, saying he was so emotional about what a group of players they are.

Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Argentina was quickly given the chance to level when Haissem Hassan tripped Nicolas Tagliafico in the box moments later. Referee François Letexier pointed to the penalty spot and Messi stepped up, but Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir dove to his left to block the shot. This was Messi's second penalty miss of the tournament after also failing from the spot against Austria in the group stage. Despite being the all-time leading scorer at World Cups, Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at the tournament. After Messi hit the post later in the half, Shobeir pulled off another great save to stop Julian Alvarez from close range.

Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Messi, 39, was in tears after the final whistle in what might be the last of his six World Cups. For much of the game, it looked like it would be a painful exit for the Argentina captain. Egypt thought it had doubled its lead in the second half when Zico finished off a sweeping attack, but the goal was disallowed after video review confirmed a foul earlier in the move. The second goal for Egypt came in the 67th minute from a similar break, and this time Zico's effort counted, but it was not enough.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in round of 16
cards.teaser: Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal as Belgium defeated the United States 4-1 on Monday night to knock the Americans out of the World Cup.
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night at Lumen Field in Seattle. De Ketelaere put Belgium ahead in the eighth minute, the first time in this year's World Cup the U.S. conceded first. Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 in the 31st minute with his second free kick goal of the tournament, energizing a largely red-white-and-blue crowd of 66,925, but De Ketelaere scored again just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. Belgium added a third goal in the 57th minute after goalkeeper Matt Freese lost control of the ball in front of his net, and second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku scored Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time.

American star Christian Pulisic injured his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt and was replaced seven minutes later. Coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying. Belgium extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games and will play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco. The U.S. failed to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930. All six CONCACAF nations have been eliminated from the tournament.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The Olympic body said in a statement after a meeting of its executive board that it stands in solidarity with the Olympic community of Ukraine, which the Olympic movement has supported since the beginning of the war and will continue to do so.

The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said. Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem, saying that decision will come at an appropriate time.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The festival is scheduled to take place in Vero Beach, bringing seafood vendors and entertainment to Indian River County for the 18th consecutive year.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the festival return on Monday. The event has become an annual tradition for the Treasure Coast region, drawing seafood lovers from across the area to sample fresh catches and local cuisine.

The festival will feature seafood from local and regional vendors. Specific dates for the November event and vendor lineup have been announced by the organizers.

Festival organizers typically host the event at Riverside Park in Vero Beach. Additional details about tickets, entertainment, and participating restaurants are expected to be released as the November dates approach.

hero.headline: FDA recalls frozen Publix GreenWise organic blueberries across eight states including Florida over E. coli risk
hero.teaser: The Food and Drug Administration issued a recall for frozen Publix GreenWise Organic Blueberries due to possible E. coli contamination. The 10-ounce packages were shipped to Publix stores in Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia.
hero.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has issued a recall for frozen Publix GreenWise Organic Blueberries sold across eight states due to possible E. coli contamination. The affected product, GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries in 10-ounce packages, was distributed to Publix retail stores throughout Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia. Consumers who purchased these blueberries are urged not to eat them and should either throw them away or return them to their place of purchase for a full refund.

The specific product under recall is frozen GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries in 10-ounce packages with lot code 60401 and a best by date of February 9, 2028. The FDA has reported 12 confirmed cases of consumers experiencing stomach illness between May 11, 2026 and June 5, 2026 that have been linked to E. coli infections. Only products matching this specific lot code and best by date are affected by the recall.

Those who consume food contaminated with E. coli can experience severe stomach cramps, diarrhea that may be bloody, and vomiting. While most healthy individuals can recover within a week, some infections can result in serious health complications. Consumers should check their freezers for the affected product and take immediate action if they have purchased the recalled blueberries.

Consumers with questions or concerns about the recall can contact the company by email at Info.foodsafety@comfrut.com or by phone at 336-899-5612. The recall affects only the specific lot of frozen organic blueberries sold at Publix stores in the eight southeastern states. Customers are reminded to check both the lot code and best by date on their packages to determine if their product is included in this recall.

cards.headline: Leon County judge sets hearing on ballot challenge that could remove GOP gubernatorial candidate James Fishback
cards.teaser: A lawsuit challenging James Fishback's eligibility to run for Florida governor moved to a fast track Tuesday when Leon County Judge David Frank scheduled a two-.
cards.body:
A lawsuit that could remove James Fishback from the Republican gubernatorial ballot moved to a fast track Tuesday when Leon County Judge David Frank scheduled a two-day hearing for July 21 and 22. Lt. Jay Collins, a rival GOP candidate, filed the lawsuit arguing Fishback does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement to run for governor. The complaint points to records tied to Fishback's voter registration and residency in Washington, D.C. Judge Frank warned attorneys there is an extreme shortage of time before the August 18 primary and noted it is likely already too late to stop ballots from being printed. Frank said if Fishback is removed, the court would issue an injunction to the Department of State directing supervisors of elections not to count votes for Fishback and to post notices. Fishback's attorney, former state representative Anthony Sabatini, told the judge the case turns on more than paperwork and that Fishback's intent will be central to determining residency.

The courtroom fight comes days after the issue erupted during last week's GOP primary debate featuring Fishback, Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner. Frontrunner Byron Donalds skipped the event but still loomed large as rivals repeatedly invoked him. During the debate, Fishback pressed Collins over the lawsuit, telling him to drop the case and later accusing Collins of trying to steal the election with Byron Donalds. Collins responded that the challenge belongs in court and that he respects the judicial system. Witness and exhibit lists are due five days before the July 21 hearing.

cards.headline: Florida median-income households need 17 months longer to save for home down payment than in 2016
cards.teaser: A new study by Smart Asset found it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians earning minimum wage of $14 an hour, it takes nearly 26 years to save for a down payment.
cards.body:
Florida ranked No. 25 on a list of states where saving for a down payment has become more difficult over the past decade, according to a new study by Smart Asset. The study found that it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians who earn a minimum wage of $14 an hour, it takes nearly 26 years to save up for a down payment on a home.

Residents in Idaho have been affected the most in the last 10 years, now needing 40 months longer to buy a home than in 2016. Only in three states, Louisiana, Mississippi and North Dakota, can median-income households save a down payment faster than they could in 2016. West Virginia has the nation's lowest down payment burden, with a median-income household needing 5.5 years to save for a down payment in 2026, just three months longer than in 2016. The report found that saving for a down payment on a minimum-wage income alone is essentially impossible in every state.

hero.headline: Vision Marine Technologies to Sell Palm City Property
hero.teaser: Vision Marine Technologies has announced plans to sell its Palm City property after consolidating operations.
hero.body:
Vision Marine Technologies completed consolidation of its tender-rigging operations at a Fort Lauderdale marina and announced the pending sale of its Palm City property. The company has moved operations from Palm City to the Fort Lauderdale location.

The consolidation involves transferring tender-rigging activities to the Fort Lauderdale marina facility. Vision Marine Technologies has entered into an agreement for the sale of the Palm City property.

The property sale in Palm City follows the company's operational restructuring in South Florida. Vision Marine Technologies completed the consolidation of its tender operations before announcing the pending real estate transaction.

The move represents a strategic reorganization of the company's Florida operations, bringing together previously separated facilities into a single location. The Fort Lauderdale marina now serves as the central hub for the company's tender-rigging business in the region.

hero.headline: St. Lucie pancreatic cancer patient Russell Reed approved for experimental treatment
hero.teaser: Russell Reed, 64, of St. Lucie County spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his oncologist believed could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective.
hero.body:
Russell Reed, 64, of St. Lucie spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his oncologist believed could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective. Reed's oncologist submitted a request through the FDA's Expanded Access Program, which can allow patients with serious or life-threatening illnesses to receive treatments outside of clinical trials when other options are limited. The pancreatic cancer patient said chemotherapy was no longer helping him at that point in his treatment.

Daraxonrasib, also known as RMC-6236, is an investigational once-daily oral pill developed by Revolution Medicines. The drug targets mutated KRAS proteins, which drive more than 90% of pancreatic cancers. While the treatment is not yet FDA-approved, early clinical trial results have generated optimism among some patients and physicians. Reed said research and clinical trial results gave him hope that daraxonrasib could help slow the progression of his disease. "There's a lot of anecdotal evidence and a lot of evidence from the clinical trials that show that this is the miracle drug for pancreatic cancer," Reed said. "It is not a cure, but it will give me time."

While waiting for an answer during the two-month period, Reed and his wife, Marnie, focused on making the most of their time together. For Marnie, the fight was never just about accessing a drug but about more family trips, more memories and more moments together. "I need someone's attention," Marnie Reed said. "The idea of sitting here and waiting for the phone to ring is not ok with me." She added that she did not want to miss a minute with her husband. "You're still here, and if you don't pay attention, you're going to miss it," she said.

Reed received the call about his approval just two days after sharing his story with WPTV. The drug is now in his hands, and his family says he is already feeling better and optimistic about what comes next. While daraxonrasib is not considered a cure for pancreatic cancer, the Reeds say the approval represents something they have been fighting for all along: more time together.

cards.headline: 28-year-old man dies after weekend shooting on South 14th Street in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after being shot multiple times early Sunday morning in Fort Pierce. Police said the shooting followed an earlier altercation on Okeechobee Road.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend, according to police. The shooting happened early Sunday morning at about 3:43 a.m. in the 300 block of South 14th Street. Police said officers arrived at the scene and found two people with apparent gunshot wounds. The 28-year-old man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a local hospital but died from his injuries on Tuesday. Officers also found a 28-year-old woman with injuries to her hand from the shooting, but her injuries were described as not life-threatening. The names of the victims have not been released.

Police said a preliminary investigation indicated that the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation in the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As they arrived home, police said a man believed to be involved in the previous altercation approached and opened fire before fleeing the area. Police said this investigation remains active and ongoing. Anyone with information in the case is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk website went down Tuesday due to third-party service provider issue
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday morning, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online around 1:30 p.m.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online by about 1:30 p.m. Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director, said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. Clavijo said as soon as he identified the issue, he had the site turned off and started the investigation. Residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage during the outage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available, with only the main page affected.

Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the outage. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider. Miller assured the public that at no time was personal or confidential information compromised or at risk, noting the clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website. The clerk's office communications team said this wasn't a hack because there wasn't any personal information compromised. Clavijo said the office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again, adding there will be a tremendous remediation as soon as they identify the exact issue.

cards.headline: Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, killed in Fort Pierce shooting on Essex Drive
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce died Tuesday after being shot at a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the victim in Tuesday afternoon's shooting on Essex Drive as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Deputies responded around 3:30 p.m. to a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned an adult man had shot another adult man with a rifle.

Deputies took the suspect into custody and began providing emergency medical care to Barnes until St. Lucie County Fire District personnel arrived. Barnes was then taken to a local hospital, where he died. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division are continuing to process evidence, conduct interviews, and work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The suspect remains in custody. Investigators say there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Legacy High School Named New Voting Location for Precinct 90 Voters in Tradition
cards.teaser: Legacy High School will serve as a new voting location for voters in Precinct 90 during the Primary Election on August 18, 2026, according to St. Lucie County Supervisor of Electio
cards.body:
Legacy High School will serve as a new voting location for voters in Precinct 90 during the Primary Election on August 18, 2026, according to St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker.

The school, located at 14505 Crosstown Parkway in Port St. Lucie, will serve voters who live north of Crosstown Parkway in the Tradition area.

Precinct 90 voters previously cast ballots at Tradition Town Hall, which is Precinct 89. Since the 2024 General Election, the voter population in the area has grown, prompting the Supervisor of Elections Office to search for an additional voting site.

Walker said the office worked with the St. Lucie County School District to secure Legacy High School as the new precinct location.

"We are grateful to the School District and Legacy High School for their commitment to serving this community," the Supervisor of Elections Office said.

The office said it is still searching for an Early Voting site to serve Tradition's rapidly growing population. Officials said the addition of Legacy High School as a precinct location is intended to help reduce Election Day wait times and ease pressure on Early Voting at the Paula A. Lewis Library.

Voters in Precinct 90 will receive mailed notifications from the Supervisor of Elections Office about the change to their assigned voting location.

For additional information, voters can contact the St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Office at 772-462-1500 or visit www.stlucievotes.gov.
